hypothesis: The parent's only crash (i130) comes from an unbounded 'no query in the required format' re-ask loop: the model sends a <guess> mid-episode while the board still has '?' cells, repeats it on every generic re-ask, and the growing conversation exceeds the 7B's 16k context. If the re-ask names the open '?' cells and says it is not time to guess, and query-less replies are capped at MISS_MAX=2 in a row (then the parent's final phase runs), the episode cannot crash this way and the model goes back to querying. Every other episode behaves exactly like the parent's.
behavior_changes: When a query-phase reply has no <query> and contains <guess> while the board has '?' cells, the re-ask lists those cells and the remaining query count, and tells the model to query one of them. The harness still does not pick the query.
After more than MISS_MAX=2 consecutive query-less replies, the query phase ends and the parent's final phase (copy the board one circuit at a time) produces the guess.
If a model call raises during the query phase (e.g. a context-length error), the query phase ends instead of crashing the episode; the final phase uses fresh short prompts.
preserved_behaviors: Deduction board from the inventory and gate rules, appended to each answer in the model's ongoing conversation
Veto of queries on already-known cells (VETO_MAX=2)
Query phase stops when the board has no '?'
Final phase: per-circuit <table> copy, rejection of tables that contradict the board or that the rules exclude, listing of <=8 allowed tables, and fallback preferring a listed table
Generic format re-ask wording when the reply simply lacks a query and is not an early guess
verification: Ran check_b1r1_cand_strict6_b10g3r2_b1r1g0.py on all 10 batch instances: status=ok and parsed_final_guess=True on 10/10 (parent: 1 crash, i130 context overflow after 41 calls).

i130 trace: the model sent an early <guess>; the new re-ask named C(1,0,0), C(1,0,1), C(1,1,0) and 9 queries left; the next reply was <query>C(1,0,0)</query>. After 11 queries the board was complete and the guess was 010101110001111100010101, which is identical to the guess from both sibling branches (b0r1g1, b1r0g2) on that instance. Total 16 calls.
The other 9 instances made the same queries and produced the same final guesses as the parent (solver cache is deterministic), so the change is inert when the failure does not occur.
risks: If the model keeps refusing to query, the episode ends with '?' cells that the final phase fills from the rule-allowed list, which may be wrong. That is still better than a crash with no guess.

Not addressed (out of conservative scope): on i253 the model spends the budget sweeping A and B row by row and ends with 3 rule-allowed tables for C. It picks 11111000, which disagrees with both siblings' picks, so at least two of the three branches are wrong there. Fixing that needs a query-allocation change, not this repair.
